note: One verdict per matrix row, written during the requirement walk. The package could show that every operation resolves and never that every requirement was designed against — 190 of 3,156 references were cited anywhere in the contracts, and the 93% coverage figure counted domains rather than requirements. This file is the evidence, and tools/check-traceability.py is what stops it becoming another hand-maintained page.
keyNote: Keyed on packageRef and xlsxRow together. Twenty-eight references name two different requirements each (CF-120), so the reference alone is not a key — see sources/requirements/reference-map.json.

verdicts.CONTRACTED: An operation or schema field demonstrably serves it.
verdicts.CONTRACTED_PARTIAL: Served, but a field, operation or state is missing. Needs a backlog entry.
verdicts.GAP_CONTRACT: Needs an operation or schema that does not exist. Needs a backlog entry.
verdicts.GAP_DECISION: Undesignable without a client answer. Needs a CF.
verdicts.ROUTED: Not a contract concern — report, configuration, permission, notification, NFR. Names its artefact class.
verdicts.PARKED: AI-parked or workshop-blocked. Names its reason rather than being skipped.
verdicts.SUPERSEDED: Duplicate of another row. Names the surviving reference.
